topics.text: Restore arid and semi-arid areas by concentrating suitable rainfall runoff and retained sediment at favourable planting locations. The aim includes vegetation recovery, soil protection and improved infiltration.
topics.title: Purpose

topics.text: Dry landscapes with usable run-on and suitable receiving soil. The book focuses particularly on Almería, with some Granada and Málaga settings. An active torrential channel requires a different level of assessment from a small hillslope basin.
topics.title: Starting landscape

topics.text: Use scattered small tree groups in favourable locations, within a retained xerophytic shrub/open matrix. Carob occurs with wild olive, palmito and lentisk. Leave unsuitable ground unplanted; do not force a uniform grid through every terrain unit.
topics.title: Vegetation arrangement

topics.text: The model addresses annual rainfall below 300 mm, with mild thermal conditions. Mojácar and Níjar examples are reported at 200–300 mm/year. Annual totals alone do not determine usable runoff, drought exposure or seedling survival.
topics.title: Reported climate context

topics.text: MR2 recommends 60 × 60 × 60 cm prepared holes, a microcatchment and stone mulch. Preparation depth differs from root-collar planting depth. Diagnose restrictions and drainage; stone structures or channel works are not automatically required for a small demonstrator.
topics.title: Soil preparation

topics.text: Rainfall capture supplements access to water; the book still allows establishment/support irrigation. Original establishment volumes are not documented for the Mojácar and Níjar reference populations. Neither provides a verified zero-water seedling protocol.
topics.title: Water

topics.text: Inspect protection, establishment success and the functioning of retention/overflow features. The model uses stone mulch and generally omits routine field fertilizer and formation pruning. Keep donor and receiving areas functioning without causing erosion elsewhere.
topics.title: Management and care

topics.text: The book discusses low overall tree densities below 100/ha, sometimes around 50/ha, alongside closer spacing inside small groups. A 6 × 6 m grid over a full hectare is about 278 trees, so that spacing cannot simultaneously mean fewer than 100 trees/ha across the same area. Donor catchment and planted patch are different areas.
topics.title: Density and its area basis

topics.title: Purpose

topics.text: Dry landscapes with usable run-on and suitable receiving soil. The book focuses particularly on Almería, with some Granada and Málaga settings. An active torrential channel requires a different level of assessment from a small hillslope basin.
topics.title: Starting landscape

topics.text: Use scattered small tree groups in favourable locations, within a retained xerophytic shrub/open matrix. Carob occurs with wild olive, palmito and lentisk. Leave unsuitable ground unplanted; do not force a uniform grid through every terrain unit.

topics.text: The model addresses annual rainfall below 300 mm, with mild thermal conditions. Mojácar and Níjar examples are reported at 200–300 mm/year. Annual totals alone do not determine usable runoff, drought exposure or seedling survival.
topics.title: Reported climate context

topics.text: MR2 recommends 60 × 60 × 60 cm prepared holes, a microcatchment and stone mulch. Preparation depth differs from root-collar planting depth. Diagnose restrictions and drainage; stone structures or channel works are not automatically required for a small demonstrator.

topics.text: Rainfall capture supplements access to water; the book still allows establishment/support irrigation. Original establishment volumes are not documented for the Mojácar and Níjar reference populations. Neither provides a verified zero-water seedling protocol.
topics.title: Water

topics.text: Inspect protection, establishment success and the functioning of retention/overflow features. The model uses stone mulch and generally omits routine field fertilizer and formation pruning. Keep donor and receiving areas functioning without causing erosion elsewhere.
topics.title: Management and care

topics.text: The book discusses low overall tree densities below 100/ha, sometimes around 50/ha, alongside closer spacing inside small groups. A 6 × 6 m grid over a full hectare is about 278 trees, so that spacing cannot simultaneously mean fewer than 100 trees/ha across the same area. Donor catchment and planted patch are different areas.
